A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmark-signature study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching the renumbered appendix sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original analyses across 32 LLMs and 88 benchmarks, including benchmark-overlap results and the appendix's comparison of perplexity granularities.

after.justification: v3 retains those original empirical results and adds leave-one-out prediction errors for the regression models and a mean-prediction baseline.

M1.justification: Thrush correlation screening, AIC forward selection, and normalized-perplexity signature comparison remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–4. The added cross-validation evaluates the existing regressions.

E1.justification: Both retain RedPajama, the 88-benchmark evaluation, and the appendix's GSM8K, MBPP, MMLU, and TruthfulQA granularity comparison. The new validation changes model splits without adding task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Section 3.2 adds an evaluated baseline that predicts each held-out model's performance using the remaining models' mean performance. The existing semantic-level and performance-level comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds leave-one-model-out validation: fit on the remaining models, predict the held-out model, repeat across models, and assess MAE. Existing benchmark metrics, preprocessing, and model configurations are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 3.2 adds a predictive robustness check asking whether the regressions predict held-out model performance better than a mean predictor. The existing granularity and benchmark-family/question-format analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v3 introduces leave-one-out resampling to estimate average predictive error. It adds no confidence intervals, seed information, or significance test for this comparison; the existing semantic-similarity bootstrap and Mann–Whitney analyses are unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 3.2 newly reports average MAE of 0.075 for the linear models and 0.180 for the mean baseline. These are additional validation results, not improvements over corresponding v1 scores. Existing results in Figures 1, 3–5 and Table 1 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The signature definition, correlation formulas, sparsity assumption, and SIS conditions remain unchanged. The SIS discussion moves from Appendix A.3 to Appendix C; no proof or mathematical derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the exposure framing from pretraining specifically to training generally, and describe the signature source as in-the-wild corpora without the pretraining qualifier. The central framework, contribution claims, and overlap conclusions remain intact.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds the explanation that regression filters error-term noise while preserving systematic relationships between benchmarks and performance. Exposure interpretations also become less pretraining-specific. Existing alternative interpretations of benchmark overlap and design misalignment are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.5 becomes Appendix E while retaining the preprocessing instructions, context length, feature-selection settings, model identifiers, vLLM configuration, evaluation harness, and two A100 80GB GPUs. No implementation or resource-access information is added.

R1.justification: The reference lists are unchanged. Related Literature moves from Appendix A.1 to Appendix A, retaining the same relationship to benchmark-agreement research and perplexity-based data selection.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited terminology edits, standardizes heading capitalization, revises author-contribution text, and reorganizes Appendix A.1–A.5 into Appendices A–E with updated cross-references. Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 receives revised styling, changes its central label from Functions from Pretraining Data to Functions from in the wild data, and shortens its caption. Appendix section breaks and some display positions change; the other figures and all four table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new validation in Section 3.2 supplies predictive evidence absent from v1, reporting MAE 0.075 against the mean baseline's 0.180. This modestly strengthens the empirical support, but token screening and selection within validation folds remain unspecified, and no uncertainty or per-benchmark errors are reported. The addition therefore does not fully resolve concerns about predictive generalization.
